# Plan of record: LLM code review for rebar via Gerrit gate + three-pass review structure

## Decisions locked
- Architecture: adopt Gerrit as the gatekeeper for code merged to rebar `main`; self-host Gerrit + rebar MCP together on AWS; GitHub as a downstream read-only mirror (Go-project topology), with GitHub `main` locked so only Gerrit's replication identity can update it. LLM review integrates as a Gerrit `LLM-Review` label gated by a submit requirement; `submitWholeTopic` lands whole reviewed features atomically. This replaced an earlier custom content-digest "review provenance" design, which the research showed reinvents what branch-protection / merge gates / Gerrit already solve.
- Review structure (ALL rebar reviews): three passes. (1) first pass emits {finding, criteria[] in locked rubric, evidence[] flexible free-text, scenarios[], impact}; (2) a SEPARATE verifier AGENT re-grounds in code and emits severity attributes {prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility} + typed BINARY verification sub-answers; (3) a DETERMINISTIC aggregator computes severity (from attributes) and validity/confidence (single conditional veto + graded fraction of binary answers) and decides block/advisory against per-criteria thresholds (project-set, start high -> mostly advisory). No model-emitted holistic severity or confidence anywhere in the decision path.
- Confidence = binary decomposition (Chain-of-Verification / FactScore / SAFE / RAGAS-faithfulness / TICK pattern), aggregated deterministically. The only veto is cited-code-reference-accuracy, applied ONLY when a code citation is present (avoids veto brittleness; supports non-citable absence findings). "is-verifiable" demoted from veto to graded signal (too subjective for a veto).
- Methodology/rubric: Google eng-practices + Anthropic security taxonomy (locked, versioned) + PR-Agent confidence/abstention discipline; Conventional Comments dropped. rebar's native finding contract kept; severity populated deterministically, not model-emitted.
- Out of scope for these epics: interactive escalation (autonomous process), threshold calibration (start high, gather dogfood data).
- Hosting: AWS is the most expensive option (~$50-70/mo); Hetzner ~$18/mo is the value leader; GerritHub free for OSS. Co-hosting Gerrit + rebar MCP on one ~8 GB box is sound (pin Gerrit heap ~2 GB, watch git GC IO spikes, no external DB via NoteDb).

## Epics created
- Infra prerequisite: d251-05e1-eb55-43b2 (AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP; GitHub main locked to Gerrit).
- Reviewer migration / three-pass framework: 9da1-cb98-2e94-4f2b.
- Agentic code-review capability (off-by-default, source-separated; dogfood on rebar): b744-4fb9-2d05-4b49. Blocked by both above.
- Comment added to plan-review epic 5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa (adopt the three-pass standard).
- Bug filed: 94a3-8bb2-5d4a-442b (tracker .gitignore omits write-lock files).

## Research basis (~14 web research spikes)
git review-provenance prior art; LLM review engines (PR-Agent/Qodo, CodeRabbit, etc.); GitHub/GitLab/Gerrit gating + merge automation (bors, merge queues, Zuul); stacked-diffs / integration-branch graduation (git seen/next/master, linux-next); Gerrit-as-gatekeeper usage (Go GerritBot, OpenStack/Zuul, Chromium CQ, Android, Qt); LLM-on-Gerrit prior art (amarula / official ai-code-review plugins); Gerrit hosting cost; severity/blocking/confidence handling across tools + 2026 research; binary-decomposed confidence (CoVe, FactScore, SAFE, RAGAS, DeepEval, TICK).

# Overlay reviewer source map — ROUND 1 (infra, testing, documentation, performance, LLM-prompts/skills)

Per-overlay criteria sources for the base+overlay code-review architecture (epics 9da1-cb98-2e94-4f2b reviewer-migration / b744-4fb9-2d05-4b49 code-review). Base = Google eng-practices (sourced). Security overlay = Anthropic claude-code-security-review (sourced). VERDICT: all 5 round-1 overlays have popular, actively-maintained, usable sources — NONE dropped. Flags below.

## Infrastructure / IaC — STRONG
- Sources (permissive): KICS 14-category taxonomy (Apache-2.0), Checkov categories (Apache-2.0), kube-linter checks (Apache-2.0), Trivy severity model (Apache-2.0); AWS Well-Architected pillars = scaffold (paraphrase).
- Meta-pattern: scanner-as-ground-truth + LLM-judge (CodeRabbit wraps Trivy/TFLint/Gitleaks). Recommend Checkov/Trivy deterministic pre-pass; overlay reasons/prioritizes vs locked rubric.
- Dimensions: IAM/least-privilege; network exposure (0.0.0.0/0, public buckets); encryption at-rest/in-transit; secrets; insecure defaults; container/k8s hardening; reliability/resource governance; logging/observability; CI/CD supply-chain (pin action SHAs); cost (advisory); structure/validity.
- Triggers: *.tf,*.tfvars,.terraform.lock.hcl; Dockerfile/Containerfile/compose; k8s/helm/kustomize (content-gate *.yaml on apiVersion+kind); CFN/SAM; *.bicep/ARM; *.rego; .github/workflows/*, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile.
- LICENSE FLAG: CIS Benchmarks = CC BY-NC-SA (NonCommercial+ShareAlike) -> DO NOT embed; use Apache-2.0 scanners (they map to CIS), cite CIS concept-only. Terrascan ARCHIVED Nov 2025, Datree EOL -> do not adopt.

## Testing — STRONG (strong deterministic trigger)
- Sources: PR-Agent relevant_tests/require_tests_review (Apache-2.0), PyNose 15-smell taxonomy (Apache-2.0), Danger "code-changed-without-tests" (MIT), mutation tools (Stryker/PIT Apache-2.0, mutmut BSD, Cosmic Ray MIT); FIRST/AAA/test-pyramid (concepts, free).
- Dimensions: presence/adequacy of tests for CHANGED behavior; right level (pyramid); edge/error/negative cases; AAA, one-assert, naming, DAMP>DRY, behavior-not-implementation; isolation/mocking discipline (no over-mock/tautological); FIRST determinism/speed (no sleep/flaky); assertion quality; test-smell taxonomy; maintainability.
- Triggers: test globs (*_test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/, tests/, src/test/**, _test.go); HIGH-VALUE deterministic: production code changed WITHOUT corresponding test change (Danger pattern); diff-coverage gate if coverage data present.
- LICENSE FLAG: tsDetect = GPL-3.0 (don't vendor code; smell NAMES/definitions are free) -> use PyNose (Apache-2.0) for the taxonomy. Google SWE book = CC BY-NC-ND (cite, don't copy/adapt prose).

## Documentation — STRONG
- Sources: Google dev-docs style guide (CC-BY-4.0, attribution), Microsoft Writing Style Guide (CC-BY-4.0), Diataxis (doc-type taxonomy), Vale + packages (MIT engine; Google pkg CC-BY-4.0), proselint (BSD)/markdownlint (MIT)/alex (MIT), PEP257/TSDoc, Keep a Changelog, CodeRabbit docstring-coverage model, Danger API-without-docs.
- Dimensions (two halves): (A) prose/docs quality — Diataxis type-fit, voice/grammar, mechanics/consistency, clarity, inclusive language, structure, examples, accessibility, correctness/freshness; (B) code-is-documented — docstring presence/completeness on public symbols, format conformance, public-API doc coverage, README adequacy, changelog entry, comment quality.
- Triggers: *.md/*.rst/docs/, README*/CHANGELOG*, docstring-heavy diffs, net-new exported symbols; HIGH-VALUE: public/exported symbol changed WITHOUT doc update (AST detect + no doc file touched).
- LICENSE FLAG: watch CC-BY-SA on some Vale style packages (share-alike). Google/MS = CC-BY (attribution, NOT copyleft). Ship an ATTRIBUTIONS note for CC-BY sources.

## Performance — STRONG sources, WEAK triggers (ESCALATION-DEPENDENT)
- Sources: Sentry performance-issue detector taxonomy (precise thresholds: N+1 DB/API, slow query >500ms, large payload, main-thread I/O, render-blocking) = concepts/facts; perflint (MIT)/Ruff PERF, Clippy perf (MIT/Apache), SpotBugs PERFORMANCE (LGPL tool; taxonomy reference), PMD optimization (BSD), Google eng-practices complexity/over-engineering (CC-BY-3.0), eslint-plugin-react-perf (MIT), Core Web Vitals.
- Dimensions: algorithmic/complexity regressions; data-access/IO amplification (N+1, chatty network, slow/unbounded query, blocking-IO-on-async) [HIGHEST signal]; allocations/copies; inefficient data structures; caching/memoization; unbounded growth/memory [high impact]; concurrency appropriateness; frontend render budgets.
- Triggers: DB/ORM/query-builder paths; loop-containing-a-call (AST = N+1); async/threadpool introductions; serialization/large-data; CURATED hot-path allowlist; frontend files.
- FLAG (TRIGGERS WEAK): perf triggers are inherently semantic — a glob tells you a file touches the DB, not that the change introduced an N+1; big-O regressions, missing memoization, unbounded growth, premature concurrency have NO reliable file/AST signature. Two-tier: deterministic triggers = recall net for the high-signal subset (N+1, blocking-IO, large-payload, render-block); rely on BASE-ESCALATION for the semantic dimensions. This overlay depends on the escalation path more than any other.
- LICENSE FLAG: Semgrep-maintained registry rules = Semgrep Rules License v1.0 (non-competing/non-SaaS) -> do NOT vendor; use perflint/Clippy/PMD.

## LLM prompts / skills — STRONG criteria, PRIMARY SOURCES PROPRIETARY (paraphrase-only)
- Sources: Anthropic prompting + skill-authoring best practices (incl. official Skill checklist) = PROPRIETARY (paraphrase only); OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 (LLM01) + Prompt-Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet = CC-BY-SA (attribution + SHARE-ALIKE); permissive tool taxonomies: promptfoo (MIT) red-team plugins, garak (Apache-2.0) probes, DSPy signatures (MIT), Inspect AI (MIT).
- Dimensions (two halves): (A) prompt/skill quality — clarity, structure/delimiting, role framing, examples/few-shot, output-format/schema, grounding/hallucination control, context-justification/conciseness, skill discovery metadata, appropriate degrees of freedom, consistency/durability, workflows/feedback loops, tool/function-def quality, eval-spec quality, calibrated emphasis (avoid over-prompting); (B) safety/injection — instruction hierarchy, segregate untrusted content, least-privilege tool scoping, HITL for high-impact, system-prompt/secret hygiene, output validation, obfuscation resistance, jailbreak/override resistance, refusal/abstention, access-control awareness (RBAC/BOLA/BFLA), adversarial test coverage.
- Triggers: *.prompt/prompts/, SKILL.md/.claude/skills//.claude/agents//*.agent.md, .cursor/rules/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/copilot-instructions, reviewers//system_prompt constants, tool-def schemas, eval specs (*.eval.*, promptfooconfig, Inspect tasks, DSPy signatures); content signals (SYSTEM_PROMPT constants, name+description frontmatter, function-schema markers).
- LICENSE FLAG: BEST sources (Anthropic/OpenAI docs) PROPRIETARY -> paraphrase, never copy. OWASP CC-BY-SA (copyleft) -> paraphrase to avoid share-alike propagation. Permissive tool taxonomies (promptfoo/garak/DSPy/Inspect) usable with notice. Author the rubric in our own words.

## Round-1 flags summary
- NONE blocked for lack of source. Per-overlay caveats: (1) Performance = weak deterministic triggers, escalation-dependent. (2) LLM-prompts/skills = strongest sources proprietary (paraphrase) + OWASP CC-BY-SA copyleft. (3) Infra = avoid CIS (NC/SA); use Apache scanners. (4) Testing = avoid tsDetect GPL code (taxonomy free); Google SWE = ND (cite). (5) Docs = watch CC-BY-SA Vale packages.
- Recurring meta-pattern across overlays: scanner/lint-as-ground-truth + LLM-as-judge. Where a permissive scanner exists, run it as a deterministic pre-pass: infra->Checkov/Trivy, docs->Vale/markdownlint, testing->coverage/Danger. Reserve LLM judgment for the semantic dimensions linters can't score.

# Overlay reviewer source map — ROUND 2 (API-compatibility, Dependencies/supply-chain, Database/migrations)

Round-2 additional overlays for the base+overlay architecture (epics 9da1-cb98-2e94-4f2b / b744-4fb9-2d05-4b49). VERDICT: all 3 strong, usable, PERMISSIVELY-licensed — NONE blocked. Common theme: no domain ships a drop-in LLM review prompt; each provides tool check-taxonomies that translate cleanly to a locked rubric (same scanner-as-ground-truth + LLM-judge meta-pattern as round 1).

## API compatibility / backwards-compat — STRONG
- Sources (all permissive): buf breaking (Apache-2.0; proto tiered WIRE/WIRE_JSON/PACKAGE/FILE), oasdiff (Apache-2.0; OpenAPI 450+ rules, ERR/WARN/INFO), graphql-js findSchemaChanges (MIT; Breaking/Dangerous/Non-breaking trichotomy), graphql-inspector (MIT; usage-aware), Griffe (ISC; Python BreakageKind enum), cargo-semver-checks (Apache/MIT; Rust), japicmp/revapi (Apache; Java source-vs-binary), @microsoft/api-extractor (MIT; TS release tags). Standards: SemVer (CC-BY), Conventional Commits (CC-BY/MIT), Google AIP-180/181/185 (Apache/CC-BY).
- Dimensions: (A) symbol existence (removal/rename=remove+add); (B) signature/shape (param removed/reordered/kind; NEW REQUIRED param = silent breaker; type change; cardinality/optionality); (C) return/output contract (narrowed return; removed response property/status code); (D) enum/closed-set (removed value=BREAKING; ADDED value=DANGEROUS); (E) wire/serialization tier (wire-safe-but-source-breaking = severity modifier; field-number reuse); (F) validation/semantics tightening (stricter validation; changed default=DANGEROUS; SAME-SIGNATURE-CHANGED-BEHAVIOR = LLM-only, NO tool catches it); (G) deprecation/versioning correctness (MAJOR bump taken? Conventional-Commits flagged? deprecation-before-removal ~90d? reserve-not-reuse).
- Severity vocab to adopt: BREAKING / DANGEROUS / NON_BREAKING / INFO (graphql-js) + ERR vs WARN (oasdiff). The DANGEROUS/WARN bucket routes to the LLM.
- Triggers: *.proto/buf.yaml; openapi*/swagger*; *.graphql/*.gql; version-field bumps; api-extractor *.api.md; *.pyi/*.d.ts/__all__ public surface. Semantic: exported-symbol diff (preferred, lower FP). Base-escalation critical for same-signature-changed-behavior, hand-rolled HTTP/RPC w/o schema artifact, config-as-API.
- LICENSE: all permissive, NO blockers. FLAGS: (a) no LLM-specific rubric exists -> author original; (b) some tools miss dims (Griffe RETURN_CHANGED_TYPE not-supported-yet; cargo-semver-checks misses signature/generics/lifetimes) -> those lean on LLM/escalation.

## Dependencies / supply-chain — STRONG
- Sources (Apache/MIT): OpenSSF Scorecard (19 checks = best taxonomy), Google OSV-Scanner, OWASP Dependency-Check, Trivy/Grype (EPSS+KEV severity), pip-audit, GitHub dependency-review-action (MIT; closest PR-time rubric); SLSA + SPDX for provenance/license.
- 7 dimensions: known vulns (CVE/OSV, weight CVSS+EPSS+KEV); malicious/typosquat/slopsquat (install scripts, obfuscation, behavioral); license compatibility (SPDX + copyleft intrusion); pinning/lockfile hygiene (hash pinning; manifest<->lockfile consistency); maintenance health (Scorecard Maintained/Contributors/Code-Review); minimal/justified additions (anti-bloat); integrity/provenance (signed releases, SBOM, SLSA).
- Triggers: all ecosystem manifest+lockfile globs (package.json/lock, requirements/poetry.lock/uv.lock, go.mod/sum, Cargo.toml/lock, Gemfile/lock, pom.xml/build.gradle, composer, *.csproj). Deterministic escalation: manifest changed WITHOUT matching lockfile change.
- LICENSE FLAGS: Snyk proprietary (concept-only); Socket product-docs (concepts not text; 403-snippet-sourced); ScanCode LicenseDB CC-BY-4.0 (attribution IF dataset embedded — avoidable via public-domain SPDX ids). NOT blocked. npm/yarn audit miss novel malware -> dim-2 must be a separate LLM-reasoned check.

## Database / migrations / SQL — STRONG
- Sources: strong_migrations (MIT; best unsafe-op->safe-rewrite), Atlas lint analyzers (Apache-2.0; 50+ DB-aware), django-migration-linter (Apache-2.0; reversibility), sqlfluff (MIT; STYLE ONLY not safety); CodeRabbit migration checks = behavior benchmark (up/down required, destructive-without-rollback, missing-migration).
- 7 dimensions: D1 destructive/irreversible (DROP; rename-as-destructive; lossy type change); D2 locking/zero-downtime (non-CONCURRENTLY index; NOT NULL+default rewrite; validating constraint scan -> NOT VALID then VALIDATE); D3 index correctness/query perf; D4 backfill/data-migration safety (batched not single-txn; fail-on-existing-rows); D5 reversibility (down-migrations; RunSQL/RunPython reverse); D6 transaction safety (CONCURRENTLY-in-txn illegal; lock/statement timeout); D7 backward-compat/expand-contract (reward expand->migrate->contract; flag single-step breaking). Optional D8 type hygiene (bigint/identity/timestamptz).
- Triggers: migrations/migrate/alembic/db-migrate/Flyway/Liquibase/prisma-migrations/drizzle/goose globs + *.sql (scope-gated) + schema files. High-value escalation: ORM model changed but NO migration file present.
- LICENSE FLAG: Squawk distributed npm/PyPI packages GPL-3.0 (Rust core MIT/Apache) -> use only as factual coverage cross-check; source wording from strong_migrations/Atlas/django-migration-linter (every Squawk rule has a permissive equivalent). pt-osc GPL-2.0 (rationale only). NO NC/SA blockers; NOT blocked.

## Round-2 flags summary
- NONE blocked. All 3 permissively sourced. Recurring: NO drop-in LLM prompt exists for any of these domains -> author the rubric from permissive tool taxonomies (facts, not copyrightable). Isolated copyleft/proprietary items each have a permissive alternative: deps Snyk/Socket(proprietary)->OSV/Scorecard/Grype; DB Squawk(GPL)->strong_migrations/Atlas; API-compat = all permissive.
- The DANGEROUS/WARN-class findings (added enum value, changed default, tightened validation, behavioral semantics) are the LLM-judgment zone routed through our pass-2 binary-verifier + pass-3 deterministic gate.

## Overlay research status: COMPLETE
Base = Google eng-practices (sourced). Overlays sourced: security (Anthropic, round 0); round 1 = infra, testing, documentation, performance, LLM-prompts/skills; round 2 = API-compat, dependencies/supply-chain, DB/migrations. All have popular, actively-maintained, usable, permissively-sourceable criteria. Next: consolidate into the per-overlay catalog entries (criteria source + license/attribution + deterministic trigger globs + base-escalation signal) for epics E2 (9da1) / E3 (b744).

# Gate correction + CI second-vote follow-on (post Opus critical-review)

## Corrections (SUPERSEDE earlier plan-of-record notes in this log)
- The v1 code gate is a SINGLE deterministic vote: the Gerrit `LLM-Review` label, cast by the deterministic pass-3 blocker on thresholds. NOT the earlier-noted three-label `Code-Review=MAX AND LLM-Review=MAX AND Verified=MAX` requirement. There is exactly ONE code-review vote in v1 — no separate human Code-Review and no CI Verified vote yet. (E1 d251 AC corrected.)
- completion_verifier is OUT OF SCOPE for the reviewer-migration epic (9da1): NOT migrated, unchanged. (E2 AC corrected.)
- The Opus critical review's endorsed must-fixes were REJECTED; the design stands. The single-vote clarification + completion_verifier-out-of-scope dissolve that review's "bots-approving-bots / who-casts-Code-Review" and "completion_verifier doesn't fit the three-pass" findings.

## Intended end state: TWO-vote gate (LLM review AND CI)
- The intended code gate requires BOTH LLM review AND CI checks (build / test / lint / format) to pass — two INDEPENDENT Gerrit votes: `LLM-Review` (v1, deterministic pass-3) + `Verified` (CI). CI integration needs more design work, so it is deferred to follow-on epic 1fa8-9db4-7c1c-48f3 ("Add CI checks as a second gate vote (Verified)"), which updates the submit requirement to `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND label:Verified=MAX AND -has:unresolved`. E4 depends_on E1 (d251) and relates_to E3 (b744).

# HANDOFF — CURRENT STATE (START HERE for a new session)

This session DESIGNED (did NOT implement) LLM code review for rebar via a Gerrit gate. NO code was written. Authoritative source = the EPICS below; this session_log is the design narrative + rationale, and where it differs from the epics the EPICS WIN (earlier entries in this log were corrected by the "Gate correction" entry and by this one).

## Epics (all open; build order follows deps)
- E1 `d251-05e1-eb55-43b2` (P1, ready): Provision AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP; lock GitHub `main` to Gerrit. [infra prerequisite]
- E2 `9da1-cb98-2e94-4f2b` (P1, ready): Realign rebar reviews to the three-pass structure; migrate the CODE-REVIEW reviewers. Holds the 11-overlay catalog (one OVERLAY CATALOG comment per overlay) + the APPROVED base->overlay escalation decision comment.
- E3 `b744-4fb9-2d05-4b49` (P1, blocked by E1+E2): Agentic code-review capability — OFF BY DEFAULT, source-separated; dogfood on rebar.
- E4 `1fa8-9db4-7c1c-48f3` (P2, blocked by E1): Follow-on — add CI checks as a SECOND gate vote (`Verified`); require BOTH LLM-Review AND CI.
- Related existing epic 5fd2-a7c2-0aec-48fa (Plan-review verification gate): carries our comment to adopt the three-pass standard + make the gate catch the "Frankenstein" and "reinventing-the-wheel" antipatterns.

## Locked design (one-liners; full detail in this log's earlier entries + the epics)
- Gate: Gerrit is the ONLY writable path to `main`; GitHub is a read-only mirror. v1 gate = a SINGLE deterministic vote: the `LLM-Review` label, cast by the deterministic pass-3 blocker on thresholds (submit requirement `label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved`). `submitWholeTopic` lands whole features atomically. The two-vote end state (LLM + CI) is epic E4.
- Review = THREE passes for all rebar CODE reviews: (1) generate evidence records {finding, criteria[] in a LOCKED rubric, evidence[] flexible free-text, scenarios[], impact} — NO model severity/confidence; (2) a SEPARATE verifier agent re-grounds in the code and emits severity ATTRIBUTES {prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility} + typed BINARY verification sub-answers {yes|no|insufficient, evidence_span}; (3) a DETERMINISTIC aggregator: conditional veto (cited-reference-accuracy, only when a citation is present) + graded fraction -> confidence; severity from attributes; block|advisory on per-criteria thresholds (start HIGH -> mostly advisory). No model-emitted holistic severity/confidence in the decision path.
- Catalog: base (Google eng-practices) + 11 overlays (security, infra, testing, docs, performance, llm-prompts, api-compat, deps, db-migrations, a11y, i18n). Each sourced from PERMISSIVE tool taxonomies (see ROUND 1 / ROUND 2 entries in this log + the per-overlay OVERLAY CATALOG comments on E2). Author every rubric in our OWN words (taxonomies are facts). Scanner-as-ground-truth + LLM-as-judge where a permissive scanner exists.
- Escalation: overlay activation = deterministic triggers UNION base-reviewer escalation (bounded enum, one-hop, per-change cap). See the APPROVED escalation comment on E2.

## Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE / deferred
- completion_verifier is NOT migrated (unchanged) — out of scope for E2.
- Threshold CALIBRATION: deferred (start high -> advisory while data is gathered).
- CI second vote (`Verified`): deferred to E4.
- No human-in-the-loop / interactive escalation (the process is autonomous, fail-to-advisory).

## Critical-review status (context for the next session)
An Opus red-team review was run and its endorsed must-fixes were REJECTED by the owner; the design STANDS. Its flagged concerns (single-box hosting/HA + signing-key co-location, advisory-forever posture, pass-2 independence, copyCondition possibly certifying an unreviewed tree, dogfood under-testing most overlays) are on record but NOT actioned — revisit only if directed.

## Bugs filed this session (rebar DX defects, separate from the design)
- 94a3 (tracker .gitignore omits lock/cache files), b156 (no non-interactive bootstrap), ab61 (init-gate inconsistency: comment vs create), eb82 (link write exits 0 without persisting when piped).

## Environment note for the next session
rebar is NOT pip-installed in this container; run it via `PYTHONPATH=src` + `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=$PWD/.tickets-tracker`, with a git worktree of `origin/tickets` at `.tickets-tracker` and a seeded `.env-id` (see bug b156). Each write may leave a stray `.ticket-write.lock` / `.graph-cache.json` in the tracker (bug 94a3) — clean before relying on git status.
